# XCNV

XCNV annotates copy-number variants and evaluates the published X-CNV
classifier without bedtools or a runtime XGBoost dependency. It also provides a
separate ACMG/ClinGen 2019 lane in which every selected criterion remains a row
that can be inspected, changed, and rescored. Every model or policy result is a
table with provider, assembly, release, identity, and explicit status metadata.

The implementation is table-oriented. DuckDB evaluates the genomic overlap and
reciprocal-overlap joins; ordinary R owns input validation, feature reduction,
the portable tree evaluator, and evidence scoring.

## Installation

```r
install.packages(
  "XCNV",
  repos = c(
    "https://rgenomicsetl.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)
```

## A real ClinVar deletion

The package includes a compact, case-limited annotation set for ClinVar allele
72461: a pathogenic deletion containing `SOX2`. This is a real scientific
example, not the synthetic fixture used by the test suite.

```{r real-case}
library(XCNV)

example <- xcnv_real_example()
example$clinvar[, c(
  "clinvar_allele_id", "clinical_significance",
  "grch38_chrom", "grch38_start1", "grch38_end1",
  "grch37_chrom", "grch37_start0", "grch37_end0"
)]
```

ClinVar publishes this record in both assemblies. X-CNV uses its GRCh37
half-open interval. When a source provides only one assembly, lift it during
resource staging—for example with Rduckhts' `rduckhts_liftover()`—and retain
the source and destination coordinates beside the case.

The following call evaluates all five X-CNV annotation families and the bundled
published model:

```{r real-prediction}
prediction <- predict_cnv(example$cnv, example$resources)
prediction[, c(
  "Chr", "Start", "End", "Type",
  "CDTS_1st", "CDTS_5th",
  "gain.freq", "loss.freq",
  "pLI", "Episcore", "GHIS", "MVP_score"
)]
```

`MVP_score` is the X-CNV model output; XCNV does not relabel it as an ACMG
criterion or clinical class. This published compatibility lane is calibrated
for GRCh37/hg19. A GRCh38 resource declaration is explicitly unsupported until
a separately validated GRCh38 model exists; XCNV never silently lifts and
relabels the result.

## Inspectable ACMG/ClinGen evidence

The same real deletion completely contains the GENCODE v19 `SOX2` gene and its
ClinGen haploinsufficiency record. The automatic provider derives only the
objective content criteria it can establish from those relations:

```{r real-evidence}
cnv <- transform(
  example$cnv,
  cnv_id = example$clinvar$cnv_id,
  cnv_type = type
)
cnv$assembly <- "GRCh37"
genes <- transform(example$genes, assembly = "GRCh37")
dosage <- transform(example$dosage, assembly = "GRCh37")
evidence <- derive_cnv_2019_evidence(cnv, genes, dosage)
evidence[, c(
  "criterion", "score", "source_id",
  "source_release", "evidence_id"
)]
```

The rows can be scored directly:

```{r real-classification}
score_cnv_2019(evidence)
```

Classification status is evaluated independently for each `(cnv_id, cnv_type)`.
Only `supported` rows receive a clinical class; unspecified, unsupported, or
conflicting assembly/status contracts return `NA` while retaining linked
evidence counts and provider/source identities. A missing `policy_id` defaults
to `acmg-clingen-2019-constitutional-cnv`; if supplied, it must be that exact,
nonempty value on every evidence row. Foreign or mixed policies fail before a
summary or classification is emitted. Evidence provider identity remains
provenance and is neither voted nor rewritten. A scalar evidence `model_id` is
based only on selected rows that contribute to the group or CNV/type score; it
is emitted only when every such row has the same nonmissing model, so an
unselected row cannot supply attribution. Conflicting nonmissing selected models
for one CNV/type are rejected. Required evidence identifiers, provenance, and
supplied contract labels must be non-missing, nonempty character/factor labels;
logical, numeric, list, and matrix values are rejected rather than stringified.
Releases are not collapsed into a misleading scalar when multiple releases
contribute.

Here criterion 2A supplies one point because the deletion completely contains
an established haploinsufficient gene. The three relations declare one coherent
assembly, and the output carries the ACMG/ClinGen policy identity separately
from any X-CNV model output. They must also use nonnegative integer BED
coordinates in the exactly representable range `[0, 2^53)` with `start < end`
and nonempty character/factor contigs without surrounding whitespace; coordinate
strings are checked before conversion. Native matching uses exact
caller/provider contig names: XCNV does not infer aliases, and a valid CNV
contig with no matching gene or dosage resource is a no-overlap result rather
than an error. A zero-row CNV relation is neutral, but nonempty CNVs require
nonempty provenance-labelled gene and dosage relations, so absent resources
never fabricate negative evidence. The `functional_biotypes` vocabulary must be explicit, nonempty,
unique character/factor labels; gene `biotype` values must be explicit and
nonempty. Both reject surrounding whitespace or placeholder tokens before
filtering.
Legitimate explicit nonfunctional Ensembl-style biotypes remain valid;
incomplete annotation cannot fabricate 1B/3A absence evidence.
The automatic provider does not invent phenotype,
inheritance, segregation, population, case-report, or partial-gene evidence.
Those require explicit additional evidence rows. DECIPHER may be used as an
optional permitted source when the user has the required access and case-level
controls; XCNV neither downloads nor bundles DECIPHER data and never infers
protected case evidence.

## Published model without XGBoost

The published classifier is one tree with 41 nodes. XCNV stores the tree as a
small, validated tabular object and evaluates it directly:

```{r model}
model <- xcnv_bundled_model()
data.frame(
  trees = length(unique(model$nodes$tree_id)),
  nodes = nrow(model$nodes),
  features = length(model$feature_names)
)

model_data <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
data("xcnv_portable_model", package = "XCNV", envir = model_data)
identical(model_data$xcnv_portable_model, model)
```

`tools/stage_xcnv_model.R` rebuilds this portable form from the original
serialized booster and compares both evaluators on 1,024 deterministic feature
rows. XGBoost is needed for that maintainer-only conversion, not for package
installation or prediction.

## Full annotation resources

The bundled real example is deliberately valid only for ClinVar allele 72461.
A general run uses a full GRCh37 resource directory:

```r
resources <- xcnv_resources("/path/to/xcnv-resources", require = "annotations")
cnvs <- read_cnv("input.bed")
predictions <- predict_cnv(cnvs, resources)
write_xcnv(predictions, "predictions.output.csv")
```

`xcnv_resource_manifest()` lists the required files. `run_xcnv()` provides the
same workflow as one call and writes only when an output path is supplied. The
current ownership and relational boundary is [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).

The compatibility contract, coordinate conventions, and current gaps are in
[`docs/upstream-compatibility.md`](https://github.com/RGenomicsETL/XCNV/blob/main/docs/upstream-compatibility.md).
